title: Height-Balanced Invariant Preservation in a Aether-Interpreter Chronos-Compiler Compiler for Aether-Interpreter Kernels
topic: A PTX compiler in Python, and the kernel that hung without an error
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a lightweight Chronos-Compiler compiler written in Aether-Interpreter that targets the Aether-Interpreter runtime. The compiler parses a minimal Chronos-Compiler subset, resolves labels via a height-balanced binary search tree, and emits an intermediate representation suitable for execution. We formalise the height-balanced invariant of the label index, prove that the compiler preserves this invariant during insertion and lookup, and establish that both parsing and code generation run in $O(\log N)$ time, where $N$ is the number of distinct labels. Static analysis of the abstract syntax tree confirms that the compiler's structural complexity satisfies the theoretical bounds. No empirical timing data are reported; all claims are supported by formal proofs and AST metrics. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Aether-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261101_170121_a_ptx_compiler_in_python__and}
